newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile officials play down February price spurt.
newsitem.headline: Chile officials play down February price spurt.

text.p: A surprisingly high 0.8 percent inflation rise in February was due to passing, seasonal factors and will not imperil the government's yearly price targets, officials said.
"For the rest of the year, we expect a gradual decline in the inflation rate, especially in the second and third quarters," Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia said.
"This is due to passing factors and does not mark a trend," he told a news conference.
Severe drought in central Chile, which has cut into farm production, has been blamed for the inflationary spurt in February.
Despite being a short month, prices jumped 0.8 percent compared to 0.5 percent in January and 0.5 percent in February 1996.

The rise brought inflation over the past 12 months to 7.2 percent, higher than the 6.6 percent seen in calendar 1996. Officials denied the numbers spelled bad news for the 5.5 percent 1997 target, which economists have already said is going to be tough to meet.

"I am...objectively confident that the inflation target will be met," said Finance Ministry adviser Jose de Gregorio, adding that an expected decline in wheat, flour, bread and fuel prices should hold down the rate later this year.
"There is no problem with wheat supplies that could bring price increases" later this year, said Garcia.
